correctness.rationale: The established exact shell counts give \(w_n(d)=n^{-1}\sum_{a=0}^dR_{n,d}(a)\), with symmetric positive factorial ratios. Their elementary product bound yields \(w_n(d)\le\min\{(d+1)/n,2/n+4/d\}\). Uniform logarithmic Taylor expansion gives the square-root profile, controlled endpoint geometric sums give \(w_n(d)\sim2/d\) when \(\sqrt n\ll d\ll n\), and harmonic-sum normalization gives the weak Uniform[1/2,1] law and moments. The own standalone program separately checks 34,152 fine triples for \(2\le n\le5\) and numeric normalization/bounds for \(n=100,400,1200\). These finite tests are corroborative only. Critical lemma assumptions d^2/n -> infinity and d/n ->0 are explicit; remaining endpoint tails decay exponentially, not assumed from experiments.

value.rationale: The output supplies a new natural large-dimensional metric statistic for a central polytope in matroid geometry: a critical square-root shell crossover with explicit integral shape and a nonconcentrating continuous log-uniform distribution. It explains the distinct inner-shell \(d/n\) and outer-shell \(2/d\) scales, yielding new typical-shell behavior not provided by finite factorial counts alone. No claims of broader geometric consequences or universal results for unrelated polytopes are made.
